Winning Creative Patterns

Split-screen + Promo creatives consistently perform best — combining price discount messaging (e.g., “55% off”) with clear product visuals drives both high SQL% and high Win%.

Hardware + Promo ads (especially when combined with “StoreHub vs Other POS” comparisons) show low CPL and CP SQL, proving that competitive framing enhances bottom-funnel efficiency.

Language localization works:
English creatives achieve highest Win%,
Chinese creatives generate good SQL%.

Underperforming Creative Patterns

Change from last quarter, Generic Unboxing videos are some of the most scalabale ads BUT (without promo or clear CTA) repeatedly underperform — they have low SQL%, low Win%, and high CPWon, indicating poor conversion efficiency.

Static or testimonial-like creatives struggle to convert despite moderate engagement — these are better suited for mid-funnel awareness than direct acquisition.

High CPL & CPSQL appear in promo-only ads without hardware context — showing that discount messaging alone is insufficient without clear product framing.

Strong Creative Drivers

Hardware-first + Promo/seasonality hybrid messaging is the most reliable top performer (e.g., Merdeka, Comic Promo, Cost Comparison).

Localized seasonal hooks (Raya, Merdeka) improve performance when paired with strong visuals and pricing incentives.

“#1 POS System” and competitive comparison messaging improve trust, driving higher SQL% and Win%.

Split-screen formats perform better than full-frame unboxing — they allow side-by-side feature or price comparisons, making the offer clearer and more engaging.

Optimization Insights

Continue scaling: Split-screen, comparison, and hardware+promo creatives (especially with localized language and price offers).

Test further: Variations of “StoreHub vs Competitor” messaging — explore visual simplification and dynamic CTA placement.

Phase out: Plain unboxing videos and testimonial content in acquisition campaigns.
